title: Repair before you replace: the ten-minute check that saves a purchase
description: A wobbly chair, a silent kettle, a torn seam. Before anything goes on the shopping list, give it ten minutes of diagnosis — many 'broken' things are one fix from fine.

body.heading: Most replacements are premature
paragraphs: Households replace things for a short list of reasons, and genuine death is only one of them. Loose screws, clogged filters, flat batteries, perished seals and simple dirt account for a surprising share of 'broken' — and every one of those is a ten-minute fix wearing a price tag.
The repair-before-you-replace habit inserts one step between 'it stopped working' and 'buy a new one': a short, honest diagnosis. Not a restoration project. Just ten minutes of looking.

body.heading: The ten-minute check
paragraphs: Ask four questions. Is it clean — filters, vents, blades, contacts? Is it connected — plugs, batteries, cables, settings? Is anything visibly loose, cracked or missing that a screw, a stitch or a spare part would solve? And does the maker or a local repairer offer the part, which the growing right-to-repair movement has made far easier to find than it used to be?

If the answer to any question is a cheap fix, do the fix and set a calendar note: if it fails again within a month, replacement has earned its place. That note stops repair from becoming endless life support for things that truly are finished.

body.heading: Know when to let go
paragraphs: Some things should not be repaired at home: anything with damaged wiring, gas appliances, safety equipment, or electrical goods that smell of burning. Those go to professionals or to recycling, without debate.
Everything else gets its ten minutes. A repaired thing carries a small pride no delivery box can match — and the money it did not cost is the quietest saving there is.

takeaway: Before replacing anything, spend ten minutes asking whether it is dirty, disconnected, loose or one spare part from fine — and let safety faults go straight to the professionals.
